trainingDropInTimetable.notes: Drop-in sessions run during term time only. No booking required.

meta.howToUse: The Project Database provides access to all equipment and resources available to our Psychology department. Use the search bar to find specific items by name, or filter by equipment type. Click on any item to view full details, including instructions, training requirements, and how to contact the psychology technician. For items requiring training, book a one-to-one session or attend our weekly drop-in support sessions.

equipmentTypes.label: Bio Physical Sensors
equipmentTypes.description: Devices that measure physiological responses such as heart rate, galvanic skin response, respiration, and EEG. These sensors capture biological signals during psychological experiments and allow researchers to examine the relationship between psychological states and bodily responses.

equipmentTypes.label: Physical Equipment
equipmentTypes.description: Tangible apparatus and equipment used in psychological research and practical sessions, including experimental apparatus, testing materials, and laboratory equipment.

equipmentTypes.label: Assessment Kits
equipmentTypes.description: Standardised psychological assessment tools and test batteries for measuring cognitive abilities, personality traits, behavioural patterns, and emotional functioning. These are professionally developed instruments used in clinical, educational, and research settings.

equipmentTypes.label: Software
equipmentTypes.description: Digital tools and applications for experimental presentation, data collection, statistical analysis, psychophysiological monitoring, and psychological assessment. Includes both standalone applications and cloud-based platforms.

equipmentTypes.label: Templates
equipmentTypes.description: Reusable digital templates typically in JSON, ZIP, Word, or Excel format containing questionnaires, experimental protocols, task designs, and survey structures for use in platforms like Gorilla, JISC Online Surveys, and Qualtrics.

trainingRequirements.label: Health & Safety Induction
trainingRequirements.description: In-person health and safety training required before use. This covers safe handling, emergency procedures, and risk awareness.

trainingRequirements.label: Tool Training
trainingRequirements.description: Specific training on how to use this equipment or software correctly, including setup, operation, and troubleshooting.

trainingRequirements.label: Professional Certification
trainingRequirements.description: Formal certification or professional qualification required for use. This may include standardised test administration credentials (e.g., WISC/WAIS) or advanced software training.

items.name: Polar H10 Heart Rate Monitor
items.description: The Polar H10 is a chest-worn heart rate sensor that provides accurate RR (inter-beat intervals) and HR (heart rate) data in real-time. It connects via Bluetooth to compatible devices and applications (phones, tablets, computers). Ideal for laboratory and field-based psychophysiological research. The sensor is water-resistant and can be used during physical activity studies.
items.useCases: Used in studies measuring cardiovascular responses to psychological stressors, emotion induction paradigms, or physical exertion. Commonly paired with Biopac for simultaneous recording of multiple psychophysiological signals. Also used in biofeedback applications and stress management training.
items.restrictions: Must be returned in good working order. Do not use with individuals who have metal implants in the chest area or are sensitive to elastic materials. Do not use on participants with broken or irritated skin at site of strap placement. Sanitise strap between participants, clean strap regularly with warm soapy water after testing session.

trainingRequired.notes: Quick 30-minute training covering pairing, data collection, and basic troubleshooting.

items.name: Biopac MP35 Data Acquisition Unit
items.description: The Biopac MP35 is a student-grade data acquisition system for recording multiple psychophysiological signals including ECG, GSR (galvanic skin response), respiration, EMG, and temperature. The R35 respiration module measures chest and abdominal breathing patterns. Works with AcqKnowledge software for real-time visualization and post-hoc analysis. Designed for laboratory research and clinical applications.
items.useCases: Essential equipment for comprehensive psychophysiological research. Used in studies of stress, emotion, anxiety, and autonomic nervous system function. Valuable for teaching psychophysiology methods to students. Can be integrated with stimulus presentation software (e.g., E-Prime, PsychoPy).
items.restrictions: Requires specialised knowledge to operate safely and correctly. Must be set up by trained personnel. Sensitive electronic equipment - handle with care. Keep away from water and electromagnetic sources. Equipment must be calibrated before use each session.

trainingRequired.notes: Comprehensive training (2-3 hours) covering setup, electrode placement, calibration, data collection, and troubleshooting. Must be completed before independent use.

items.name: WAIS-IV (Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale - 4th Edition)
items.description: The WAIS-IV is a comprehensive standardised assessment of cognitive abilities for adults aged 16-90 years. It measures four major index scores: Verbal Comprehension (vocabulary, similarities, information), Perceptual Reasoning (block design, matrix reasoning, visual puzzles), Working Memory (digit span, arithmetic), and Processing Speed (symbol search, coding). Provides a Full Scale IQ score. This is a restricted assessment tool with strict security and ethical requirements.
items.useCases: Used for clinical assessment, neuropsychological evaluation, educational assessment, and research into cognitive functioning. Particularly useful in identifying cognitive strengths and weaknesses, assessing for intellectual disability or giftedness, and evaluating effects of brain injury or neurodegenerative conditions.
items.restrictions: **RESTRICTED ASSESSMENT TOOL** - Only to be used by trained and accredited practitioners with appropriate qualifications in psychological or educational assessment. Cannot be used on individuals under 16 years old. Test materials must remain secure and confidential at all times. All scoring and interpretation must be carried out by qualified personnel. Test kits must not be left unattended. Photocopying or reproducing test materials is strictly prohibited.

items.name: Gorilla Experimental Builder (Software License)
items.description: Gorilla is a cloud-based platform for creating and running psychological experiments, including surveys, reaction-time tasks, cognitive tests, and questionnaire studies. No programming required - build experiments using a drag-and-drop interface. Supports data collection from diverse participant pools, real-time visualisation, and export to multiple statistical formats. Accessible from any device with a web browser.
items.useCases: Ideal for running studies during remote learning periods. Supports lab-based data collection when paired with participant management tools. Used for teaching experimental design to students. Useful for cross-national or international studies. Can integrate stimulus presentation with data collection and analysis.
items.restrictions: Access requires institutional license login. Data must be stored securely in compliance with data protection regulations (GDPR). Only use for approved research protocols. Do not share login credentials. Session data should be downloaded and stored locally regularly.

trainingRequired.notes: Introductory tutorials available on platform. For advanced features, attend drop-in sessions or request one-to-one support.

items.name: OQ-45 Therapy Outcome Measure Template (Gorilla)
items.description: Pre-built Gorilla experiment template implementing the OQ-45.2 (Outcome Questionnaire-45), a widely-used 45-item self-report measure of psychological distress and functioning. Template includes automated scoring, result feedback, and data export. Customisable for different research or clinical applications.
items.useCases: Used for measuring psychotherapy outcomes, monitoring treatment progress in clinical settings, and research on psychological intervention effectiveness. Useful as a teaching tool for introducing outcome measurement in psychology education.
items.restrictions: Use only for appropriately trained clinicians or researchers. Ensure informed consent obtained from all participants. Maintain confidentiality of participant responses. Delete data securely after research completion if required by ethics protocol.

trainingRequired.notes: Demonstrates how to customise Gorilla templates. 15-20 minute overview in drop-in sessions.

items.name: Clicker Counters
items.description: A clicker counter is a small handheld device with a button and a number display. Every press adds one to the count, letting you tally how often something happens without having to stop and write it down.
items.useCases: Handy any time you need to count events as they happen. Students often use them to record how frequently a particular behaviour occurs during an observation, to keep a running tally while watching video footage, or to help someone self-monitor a habit by clicking each time they notice themselves doing it. Because they're simple and cheap, they work well for group projects where several people are counting at once.

items.name: Stopwatches
items.description: A simple, precise timing device that measures how long something takes. It can capture both how long a behaviour lasts (duration) and the gap before a response begins (reaction/latency).
items.useCases: Useful anywhere timing matters. Students use stopwatches to time how long participants take on a task, to measure reaction times in simple demonstrations, or to structure timed conditions in an experiment. They're a reliable, low-tech option when you don't need software-level precision.

items.name: Sony WH-CH720N Noise Cancelling Headphones
items.description: Comfortable over-ear headphones with optional noise cancelling, giving clear sound and a quiet listening environment.
items.useCases: Good for anything involving sound. Students use them to play audio stimuli to participants under consistent, distraction-free conditions, or to review and transcribe recordings of interviews and focus groups. The noise cancelling helps keep listening conditions the same for everyone taking part.

items.name: Rulers
items.description: A standard 30cm clear plastic ruler with millimetre markings.
items.useCases: A general-purpose measuring tool for setting up apparatus, marking distances, or measuring small objects and stimuli. It can also be used for a classic ruler-drop reaction time demonstration, where you catch a falling ruler and convert the distance into a response time.

items.name: Mini Wright Peak Flow Meter
items.description: A small handheld device that measures peak flow — how fast a person can blow air out of their lungs in a single hard breath. The reading gives a simple snapshot of breathing strength.
items.useCases: Useful in studies that touch on breathing and the body's response to stress. Students might use it to explore how anxiety or arousal affects breathing, to see whether a relaxation or breathing exercise changes lung performance, or to add a simple physical measure alongside self-report data on mood or wellbeing.

items.name: Ishihara Colour Blind Test 38 plate
items.description: A set of 38 coloured 'dot' plates, each containing a hidden number that's easy to see with typical colour vision but hard to read for people with red-green colour deficiency. A quick, well-established way to check colour vision.
items.useCases: Often used as a screening step. Students include it to check that participants can see colour normally before a task that relies on colour, so colour vision doesn't accidentally influence the results. It can also be the focus of a study in its own right when looking at individual differences in perception.

items.name: Snellen 3m Chart
items.description: A compact eye chart with rows of letters that get smaller down the page, used to measure visual acuity (how sharp someone's vision is) from a set distance of 3 metres.
items.useCases: A simple way to check how clearly participants can see. Students use it to screen vision before tasks that depend on reading or spotting visual detail, or as a straightforward measure of visual acuity in a wider study.

items.name: Drager Alcotests 6000
items.description: A professional-grade digital breathalyser that estimates blood alcohol concentration (BAC) from a breath sample. It's the same class of device used by police, giving a fast and accurate reading.
items.useCases: Used where alcohol is a variable of interest. Students might use it to confirm participants are sober before testing, or in supervised studies looking at how alcohol relates to things like reaction time, decision-making, or risk-taking. A single-use mouthpiece is needed for each reading.

items.name: Drager Alcotest 6000 Mouthpieces
items.description: Single-use hygienic mouthpieces for the Drager Alcotest 6000 breathalyser. A fresh one is used for each participant.
items.useCases: Required consumable for taking a breath reading with the Drager Alcotest 6000. Fit a new mouthpiece for every person to keep readings hygienic.

items.name: Bedfont piCO™ Smokerlyzer®
items.description: A handheld monitor that measures the amount of carbon monoxide (CO) in a person's breath. Because smoking raises breath CO, it gives an objective check of recent smoking rather than relying on what someone reports.
items.useCases: Useful in research on smoking and health behaviour. Students use it to check smoking status objectively, to include or exclude participants based on CO level, or to track progress over time in studies of quitting or cutting down. Needs a d-piece and a fresh mouthpiece for each reading.

items.name: Pico D-Pieces
items.description: A small adapter that connects the SteriBreath mouthpieces to the Pico Smokerlyzer, forming the path the breath sample travels through.
items.useCases: Required part for taking a reading with the Pico Smokerlyzer. It links the mouthpiece to the monitor so a breath sample can be measured.

items.name: SteriBreath Mouth Pieces
items.description: Single-use hygienic mouthpieces used with the Pico Smokerlyzer and its d-piece to take a breath carbon monoxide reading.
items.useCases: Required consumable for the Pico Smokerlyzer. Use a fresh mouthpiece for every participant to keep readings clean and hygienic.

items.name: Tape Measures
items.description: Flexible fabric tape measures for taking body or object measurements that a rigid ruler can't easily manage.
items.useCases: Useful whenever you need to measure around or along something. Students use them for body measurements such as waist, neck or limb circumference in health-related studies, or to measure short distances when setting up a task or apparatus.

items.name: Darwin Taste Strips
items.description: Small paper strips treated with a harmless test substance that some people taste strongly and others barely notice. They offer a quick way to explore individual differences in taste sensitivity.
items.useCases: A simple tool for studies on taste and individual differences. Students might use them to see how sensitive someone is to certain tastes and link that to things like food preferences, willingness to try new foods, or sensation-seeking. Because taste sensitivity varies a lot between people, they're a nice hands-on way to demonstrate individual variation.

items.name: Digitial voice recorders
items.description: Small pocket-sized digital voice recorders that capture clear audio and transfer easily to a computer.
items.useCases: Ideal for capturing spoken data. Students use them to record one-to-one interviews and focus groups for later transcription, or as a quick way to make audio notes in the field. Always get participant consent before recording.

items.name: Body Fat Callipers
items.description: Handheld mechanical calipers that measure the thickness of a skin fold at set points on the body, giving an estimate of body fat.
items.useCases: Used in health and wellbeing research where body composition is relevant. Students might include caliper readings alongside other measures when studying topics like body image, health behaviour, or the physical effects of an intervention. Measurements should be taken sensitively and with clear consent.

items.name: OMRON M2 Basic Automatic Blood Pressure Monitor
items.description: A clinically validated automatic monitor that wraps around the upper arm and measures blood pressure (systolic and diastolic) along with pulse, at the press of a button.
items.useCases: A go-to measure for studies involving stress and the body. Students use it to see how blood pressure and heart rate respond to a stressful or emotional task, to track changes during relaxation or biofeedback, or as a physical measure to sit alongside self-report data. Quick and non-invasive, so it fits easily into many designs.

items.name: Brannan Clinical Thermometer
items.description: A precise medical-grade thermometer for measuring body temperature quickly and reliably.
items.useCases: Useful when body temperature is a variable of interest. Small shifts in temperature can accompany stress, arousal, or the body's daily rhythms, so students might use it as a simple physical measure in studies on stress responses, alertness, or time-of-day effects.

items.name: Aesthesiometer
items.description: A precise handheld tool with two adjustable points, used to test touch sensitivity by measuring the smallest distance at which a person can still feel two separate points rather than one (the 'two-point threshold').
items.useCases: A classic tool for exploring the sense of touch. Students use it to map how touch sensitivity differs across parts of the body (fingertips versus the back, for example), to demonstrate how the somatosensory system works, or in studies comparing sensory sensitivity between people or conditions.

items.name: WISC-V
items.description:
The Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children – Fifth Edition (WISC-V) is a widely used, individually administered test of cognitive ability for children aged 6 to 16. It gives an overall picture of intellectual functioning as well as scores across several areas.

It measures:
- Verbal Comprehension: vocabulary, verbal reasoning, and understanding of concepts.
- Visual Spatial: judging visual detail and spatial relationships.
- Fluid Reasoning: logical problem-solving and spotting patterns.
- Working Memory: holding and working with information in mind.
- Processing Speed: how quickly and accurately simple visual tasks are completed.
items.useCases: A cornerstone tool for studying and assessing children's cognitive development. Used in research and training on intelligence, learning, and individual differences, and in supervised assessment work. As a restricted, standardised test it can only be administered by suitably trained and qualified people.

items.name: WRAT-5
items.description:
The Wide Range Achievement Test – Fifth Edition (WRAT-5) is an efficient, standardised test of core academic skills — reading, spelling and maths — suitable for ages 5 through to adulthood. It gives a quick, reliable snapshot of foundational attainment.

It measures:
- Word Reading: reading individual words aloud, tapping decoding and sight-word recognition.
- Sentence Comprehension: understanding written sentences using a fill-in-the-blank format.
- Spelling: spelling dictated words correctly.
- Maths Computation: number skills from basic arithmetic up to more advanced problems.
items.useCases: Useful in research and training on literacy, numeracy, and learning differences, and as a quick attainment screen in wider studies. Being norm-referenced, it lets scores be compared against a representative sample. It should be administered by appropriately trained people.

items.name: Minnesota Dexterity Task
items.description: The Minnesota Manual Dexterity Test is a standardised, board-and-discs apparatus that measures hand-eye coordination and how quickly and smoothly a person can move and place objects with one or both hands.
items.useCases: A practical tool for studying motor skill and coordination. Students might use it to measure fine motor performance, to see how factors like stress, fatigue, or practice affect dexterity, or to track improvement across repeated attempts.

items.name: CTOPP-2
items.description:
The Comprehensive Test of Phonological Processing – Second Edition (CTOPP-2) is a standardised test of the sound-based skills that underpin reading. It's widely used in research and assessment around literacy and language development.

It measures:
- Phonological Awareness: noticing and manipulating the individual sounds within spoken words.
- Phonological Memory: briefly holding sound-based information in mind.
- Rapid Naming: how quickly familiar items (like letters or numbers) can be named.
items.useCases: Useful in research and training on reading development, literacy difficulties such as dyslexia, and language processing. It's often used to understand the building blocks of reading, and should be administered by appropriately trained people.

items.name: TOWRE-2
items.description:
The Test of Word Reading Efficiency – Second Edition (TOWRE-2) is a quick, standardised measure of how accurately and fluently a person can read printed words under time pressure, for ages 6 to 24.

It measures:
- Sight Word Efficiency: reading real words rapidly and accurately.
- Phonemic Decoding Efficiency: sounding out made-up 'nonsense' words rapidly, which isolates pure decoding skill.
items.useCases: A handy tool for research and assessment on reading fluency and literacy difficulties. Because it's quick to run, it works well as a reading measure within a larger study, or for tracking reading efficiency over time. Should be administered by appropriately trained people.
